content: Nicotine gum is prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking. It serves as a substitute for the oral activity associated with smoking and provides a controlled source of nicotine to alleviate withdrawal symptoms that occur when smoking cessation begins. Nicotine gum is intended for oral use and should be chewed, not swallowed. Follow the instructions on the product label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the gum exactly as directed. Do not use more or less than prescribed, and do not use it more frequently unless instructed by your doctor. Typically, treatment begins with the 2-mg gum. However, heavy smokers (those smoking more than 25 cigarettes per day) may start with the 4-mg gum. Nicotine gum can be used regularly by chewing one piece every 1–2 hours initially, or it can be used as needed when you feel the urge to smoke. Chew the gum slowly until you taste nicotine or feel a slight tingling sensation in your mouth. Then stop chewing and park the gum between your cheek and gum. When the tingling subsides (after about 1 minute), start chewing again. Repeat this process for about 30 minutes. Avoid chewing the gum too quickly, chewing more than one piece at a time, or chewing another piece too soon after the first. If you are using the 2-mg gum, do not exceed 30 pieces per day under medical supervision or 24 pieces per day without supervision. If you are using the 4-mg gum, do not exceed 24 pieces per day. After 2–3 months, gradually reduce the amount of nicotine gum you use to prevent withdrawal symptoms. Suggested strategies for reducing use include: Decreasing the total number of pieces used per day by one piece every 4–7 days. Reducing the chewing time for each piece from 30 minutes to 10–15 minutes over 4–7 days, then gradually decreasing the total number of pieces used per day. Substituting one or more pieces of sugarless gum for nicotine gum, increasing the number of sugarless gum pieces substituted every 4–7 days. Replacing 4-mg gum with 2-mg gum and applying the above steps. Considering stopping nicotine gum use entirely when your cravings are satisfied with one or two pieces per day. Using nicotine gum for longer than 3 months is discouraged. Do not use it for more than 6 months without consulting your doctor. Before using nicotine gum, inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially acetaminophen (Tylenol), caffeine, diuretics (water pills), imipramine (Tofranil), insulin, medications for high blood pressure, oxazepam (Serax), pentazocine (Talwin, Talwin NX, Talacen), propoxyphene (Darvon, E-Lor), propranolol (Inderal), theophylline (Theo-Dur), and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had a heart attack, irregular heart rhythm, angina, ulcers, uncontrolled high blood pressure, overactive thyroid, pheochromocytoma, or any dental conditions or disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using nicotine gum, stop using it and contact your doctor immediately, as nicotine and nicotine gum can harm the fetus. Do not smoke cigarettes or use other nicotine products while using nicotine gum, as this can lead to nicotine overdose. Avoid eating or drinking, especially acidic beverages like coffee or soft drinks, for 15 minutes before and during the use of nicotine gum to ensure proper nicotine absorption. Nicotine gum may cause mild side effects. Contact your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Mouth ulcers Jaw muscle aches Dizziness Headache Upset stomach If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Seizures Heart rhythm disturbances Difficulty breathing In the event of a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store nicotine gum in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused gum properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
